intro: Progress turns honest logs into trends. Days are noisy; weeks and months show direction — protein, weight, and adherence included.
buddyTip: Open Progress weekly with one question: “What did good days share?” Change one variable afterward.
mission: Open Progress, scan the last week, and write one keep / one change note.
why: Without Progress, Foodiary is a pile of receipts. Trends reveal whether your energy budget, protein anchors, and habits are working under real life.
Daily obsession with a single weigh-in creates false emergencies. Progress exists to zoom out so you can coach calmly.
Progress only works if logs are honest and complete enough. Capture on Home; correct in Foodiary; learn here.
Progress is also where you notice skill gains: fewer blank days, better restaurant estimates, steadier protein. Those wins deserve equal attention beside the scale.

points: Links back to Foodiary for cause-finding

misconceptions.myth: Progress at 0 means the app is broken.
misconceptions.truth: Often missing kcal on rows, wrong day selected, or logging only in empty Foodiary placeholders. Check the Quick Guide path.

misconceptions.myth: I should change five targets every time Progress looks messy.
misconceptions.truth: Multi-change weeks teach nothing. Adjust one lever.

steps: Ensure the week has enough Home logs with nutrition
Open Progress; note direction, not drama
Tap into odd days via Foodiary context
Set one theme for next week
Return to daily ritual — don’t live inside charts
how.buddyHelps: Buddy capture feeds Progress. Coaching quality rises when trends reflect real restaurants, travel, and training — not curated highlights.

sections.title: Reading weight
paras: Prefer multi-day or weekly trends. Sodium, carbs, and hormones move water. Fat change is slower.

sections.title: Reading protein
paras: Count how often anchors appeared. Two heroic protein days don’t cancel five low ones for how the week felt.

sections.title: Monthly zoom
paras: Once a month, widen the window. Ask whether goals still fit life, then change at most one target. Archive a win in writing so memory does not erase it.

mistakes.quote: I judged my whole program on this morning’s weigh-in.
mistakes.why: Use Progress trends. One morning is weather, not climate.

mistakes.quote: Progress looked bad so I deleted old logs.
mistakes.why: Deleting erases learning. Keep honesty; adjust forward.

mistakes.quote: I only check Progress when I feel guilty.
mistakes.why: Scheduled calm reviews beat shame-triggered chart spirals.

encouragement: Progress is a mirror for patterns, not a verdict on your worth. Log honestly, review weekly, improve once — repeat.
